paragraphs: Suited to people willing to get acceptance, weighing, charging, receipts, and handover right item by item at the counter, who can then trial postal service clerk work. Understanding service requirements, verifying the appearance and destination of mail, and pausing a quote when information is missing is closer to the daily tasks than simply liking to talk with people. USPS position conditions and Chinese position requirements must each be checked in their own announcements.

Observable signals: keeping verification habits while queuing and repeating tasks; willingness to explain the basis for postage and the scope of what can be handled; and re-checking and escalating first when the address, weight, service type, or payment information is inconsistent. If you reject procedures, records, or standing and lifting, observe a real branch first.

Safe trial: using the fully fictional A1–A3 three pieces of mail and the exercise charging table on this page, write the counter acceptance and handover record within 45 minutes. A1 and A2 can be counted in exercise points, and A3 
has a missing destination and must be marked pending confirmation; real names, addresses, postage, or orders must not be used.

Self-check three points: A1 should be 9 exercise points, A2 should be 23 exercise points, and the confirmed subtotal is 32 points; A3 is missing a destination and no total price may be invented; the handover note must state the information to be verified, the responsible person, and the next step, and must not promise a delivery time on your own.

If you are willing to switch between customer communication, rule verification, and physical mail handling and can keep traceable records reliably, you can trial the postal counter direction. If you prefer outdoor delivery, central sorting, or customer service advice, compare the corresponding occupations' tasks and position conditions, and do not infer a direct transfer from the name.

This page covers only the counter acceptance, postage transaction, mail checking, and sorting-related work of US O*NET 43-5051.00 Postal Service Clerks. Chinese postal branches may use different position titles; service authority, charges, user information handling, and recruitment conditions follow local law and institutional rules and are not automatically determined by a US occupational code.

The core tasks of O*NET 43-5051.00 include weighing and calculating postage by type, weight, and destination, verifying mail postage and appearance, selling stamps and postal products, and accepting and sorting mail. Its page employment column uses an older projection period; the 2025–2035 figures, change, and openings on this page follow BLS Table 1.2 instead.

entries: Acceptance confirmation｜ask about the mail type, destination, and required service｜check the scope of what can be handled and the required information, clarify first when the address or service option is missing, and do not quote postage from appearance alone.

Weighing and charging｜calculate by mail weight, dimensions, destination, and service option｜use the agency's current postage and system to verify the amount; the fictional exercise points on this page are not real postage.

Mail verification｜check packaging, labels, postage, and mailing conditions｜when appearance, address, or rule questions appear, pause the affected steps and hand them to authorized personnel for confirmation.

Counter transactions｜sell stamps and other postal products and handle payments｜provide a receipt or voucher, verify the payment against the system record, and do not adjust standards or promise extra services on your own.
Sorting and handover｜route mail by destination and service category｜record the item count, scan status, and unfinished items, and hand anomalies to the next stage.

Confidentiality and traceability｜protect user names, addresses, and mailing information｜use the material only in authorized systems and within the position's scope, and handle misdirected items, complaints, and corrections per agency procedures.

values: Material setup｜all editorially fictional

The practice outlet uses a fictional point schedule: the first band for standard letters ≤100 grams is 9 points; over 100 grams up to 500 grams is 23 points. For arithmetic practice only, not real postage or service rules.

A1: same-city standard letter 80 grams, complete address, first band selected; should count 9 points. A2: out-of-town standard letter 320 grams, complete address, second band selected; should count 23 points.
A3: parcel 1.2 kilograms, destination missing; this table has no parcel band, so no quote can be given. All three use fictional names and addresses; real customer data must not be entered.
Task and deliverable｜45 minutes

0–5 minutes read the materials; 5–20 minutes build a three-row table listing category, weight, destination, band, known points, unknown items and next step; 20–30 minutes recalculate independently; 30–40 minutes write the A3 clarification and customer explanation; 40–45 minutes review and revise against the rubric below.

For A3, at minimum clarify the destination and the selected service, then check the applicable parcel rate with an authorized supervisor; write down what is pending confirmation, the handling role and the next step, and do not enter real names or addresses.
Reference answer and customer explanation

A1｜standard letter｜80 grams｜same city, complete address｜≤100 grams｜9 points｜band information complete｜record according to exercise rules. A2｜standard letter｜320 grams｜out of town, complete address｜100<weight≤500 grams｜23 points｜band information complete｜recheck label. A3｜parcel｜1.2 kilograms=1200 grams｜destination missing｜parcel band not provided｜unknown｜destination, service and parcel rate pending check｜pause quoting and refer to authorized supervisor.

Confirmed subtotal 9+23=32 points, covering only A1+A2; the total price for three items is unknown, and A3 unknown does not equal 0. The points are editorially fictional and cannot be converted into CNY or USD postage.

Customer explanation example: the subtotal for the first two letters in the practice table is 32 points. The third item is a parcel and needs a destination and service option added, and the current table has no parcel rate. I will first ask an authorized supervisor to verify; before confirmation, no fee or acceptance can be promised.
Review rubric｜editorial self-assessment, not an employer examination

Four items scored 0–2 each, total 0–8: (a) bands and units: 2 points if the 80 gram and 320 gram bands and the 1200 gram conversion are all correct, 1 point if partly correct, 0 points if the wrong band is applied; (b) arithmetic and scope: 2 points if 9, 23 and 32 are correct and limited to A1+A2, 1 point if the arithmetic is right but the subtotal scope is unclear, 0 points if 32 is reported as the total for three items.

(c) missing items and authority: 2 points for asking about destination and service, pointing out that there is no parcel band and pausing to escalate, 1 point for pointing out only some missing items, 0 points for guessing the A3 fee; (d) explanation and records: 2 points if the customer explanation clearly marks the fictional points, the unknown and the handover role, 1 point if one item is missed, 0 points if real customer data is used or an actual fee is promised.

Error example: A3 reuses the letter second band of 23 points and reports 55 points for three items. Score 0／0／0／0=0 points; first delete the guessed amount, restore the A3 unknown and the 32-point subtotal, then add the clarification and handover. subject.name: Postal Service Clerks
subject.summary: Postal service clerks accept mail and parcels at the post office counter, weigh items and verify postage, handle stamp and other postal product transactions, check mail status, and sort or hand over mail by destination. Accurate charging, protecting user information, pausing on anomalous items, and escalating per agency procedures are key responsibilities; USPS position conditions and Chinese postal institution requirements must be verified separately.
